planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost, since chinense superhots germinate slowly in cool soil.

directions: King Naga is a large-podded Naga-type superhot producing elongated, slightly wrinkled fruit that ripens from green to red and can grow longer than most of its Bhut Jolokia and Naga Morich relatives. Flavor and heat are similar to Naga Morich, with a fruity edge beneath the intense capsaicin load. Give plants a long, warm growing season, rich well-drained soil, and even moisture, since irregular watering causes blossom drop on chinense superhots. Stake or cage plants as pod clusters grow heavy, and wear gloves when harvesting ripe fruit.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost; this Trinidad strain is slow to establish in cool conditions.

directions: 7 Pot Lava is a Trinidad heirloom superhot bearing rounder, less deeply wrinkled pods than classic 7 Pot strains, ripening through a mottled green-to-orange stage before finishing a glowing red-orange reminiscent of molten lava. The flavor carries a fruity sweetness alongside ferocious, lingering heat prized by hot sauce and extract makers. Provide a long hot season, consistent watering, and staking once fruit clusters weigh down the brittle branches. Handle ripe pods with gloves, since the oils cling stubbornly to skin.

planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost; this rare Trinidad strain needs a full hot season to size up and ripen.

directions: 7 Pot Giant is an uncommon Trinidad superhot grown for unusually large, bumpy pods that ripen from green to a deep glossy red, bulkier than most other named 7 Pot strains. Collectors value it for crossbreeding and for its exceptionally heavy capsaicin load relative to its pod size. Grow in full sun with rich, well-drained soil and steady moisture, since blossom drop is common under water stress in chinense superhots. Wear gloves and eye protection when handling and processing ripe fruit.
sources: Chile Pepper Institute, New Mexico State University

planting.note: Start seed indoors on a heat mat 8-10 weeks before the last frost, since this superhot strain is slow to germinate in cool soil.

directions: 7 Pot Cinder produces bumpy, classically wrinkled pods that shift from fluorescent green through caramel tones to a smoky, rust-red finish resembling a cooling cinder. Beneath its floral, fruity aroma lies an exceptionally intense, slow-building heat even by superhot standards. Plants grow vigorously and set fruit heavily given a long warm season, full sun, and even soil moisture. Stake plants to support heavy pod clusters and use gloves when harvesting, as the capsaicin oils are very persistent on skin.
